heuristics.rule: Email a professor directly before applying to confirm they are accepting new students
heuristics.condition: When identifying potential PhD advisors through school websites...
heuristics.action: Send a cold email (套磁) to gauge interest and confirm available slots before investing application effort
heuristics.because: Not every professor accepts new students each cycle, and spots are typically limited — confirmed by the commenter as common practice

decision_factors.why_it_matters: A professor may be a perfect research fit but have no open slots, making the application futile regardless of qualifications
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Direct email outreach before or during application season to ask explicitly about availability

failure_patterns.pattern: Applying to advisors without confirming they are accepting students
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Applicants assume any listed faculty member on a department website is automatically recruiting — the website rarely flags closed labs
failure_patterns.consequence: Wasted application fees and time; no response or automatic rejection due to advisor having no capacity
warning_signs: Applicant lists professors solely based on research topic match without any prior contact
Applicant sends mass applications without personalization or prior outreach

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you confirmed that your target advisor is actively recruiting new PhD students this cycle?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the application is viable regardless of research fit or qualifications
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Proceed with tailored application materials; reference the communication in your SOP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Send a 套磁 email first before committing application resources to that program

industry_realities.common_belief: Any professor listed on a department website is available to take new PhD students
industry_realities.actual_reality: Professors have limited student quotas and may not be recruiting in a given year; availability must be confirmed directly
industry_realities.implication: Applicants should treat advisor availability verification as a prerequisite step, not an afterthought

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Searches school rankings or professor profiles, finds research fit, applies directly without contact
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Uses research fit as a first filter, then proactively emails shortlisted professors to confirm availability and gauge mutual interest before finalizing application list
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Skipping pre-contact wastes application resources on labs that are not recruiting and misses the signal-value of a warm reply that increases admission probability

community_misconceptions.misconception: Using an AI-powered bulk matching service that generates 50+ advisor leads will significantly improve your admission outcomes
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The framing borrows legitimacy from 'big data' and 'AI' language and promises efficiency gains over manual search, which appeals to time-pressured applicants
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: PhD admission is fundamentally relationship-driven; a small number of well-researched, personalized outreach emails to genuinely relevant advisors outperforms mass-matched cold contacts in both reply rate and admission success
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Applicants pay for a service that generates low-quality, potentially outdated leads; mass 套磁 emails signal lack of genuine interest to professors and reduce reply rates

psychological_barriers.trigger: Applicant feels overwhelmed by the scale of the advisor search and turns to bulk AI matching services
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Decision paralysis and fear of missing a better option — the search space feels unmanageable so any system that promises to handle it feels reassuring
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Outsourcing the selection process entirely to a third-party tool or agency rather than doing targeted research, mistaking volume of leads for quality of fit
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the task: PhD advisor selection is not a search problem to be solved by coverage — it is a fit problem solved by depth. Narrow to 5–10 genuinely relevant professors and invest in understanding their recent work before any outreach.
